test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 09 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is corrosion most commonly observed as?

options.text: Boiling of water in a kettle

solution:
The correct answer is __**Rust formation on iron objects**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Corrosion** is a natural process that converts a refined **metal** into a more chemically stable form such as **oxide**, **hydroxide**, or **sulfide**. It is the gradual destruction of materials by chemical and/or electrochemical reaction with their environment.
 
• **Rusting** is the most common form of corrosion observed in daily life, specifically occurring on **iron** and its **alloys** like **steel**. It occurs when **iron** reacts with **oxygen** and **moisture** (water) in the air to form **hydrated ferric oxide**. ***Hence, the statement regarding rust formation is correct.***
 
• The chemical formula for **rust** is **Fe2O3·nH2O**. This reddish-brown flaky substance weakens the **structural integrity** of the **metal**, leading to significant **economic loss** and safety hazards in **bridges**, **buildings**, and **vehicles**.
 
• **Glowing of a bulb** is a physical process where the **filament** (usually **tungsten**) gets heated to a high temperature and emits **light**. It does not involve the chemical degradation of the metal in the way corrosion does. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Boiling of water** is a **physical change** or phase transition from **liquid** to **gas** occurring at **100 degrees Celsius** (at standard pressure). It is not related to the chemical corrosion of metals. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***
 
• **Melting of metal** is also a **physical change** where a solid metal turns into a **liquid** state upon reaching its **melting point**. While high temperatures can accelerate corrosion, melting itself is not corrosion. ***Hence, this statement is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Types of Corrosion in Other Metals:**

 
 
• **Silver Tarnish:** When **silver** objects are exposed to air containing **hydrogen sulfide**, they develop a black coating of **silver sulfide (Ag2S)**.
 
• **Copper Verdigris:** **Copper** reacts with moist **carbon dioxide** in the air to slowly lose its shiny brown surface and gain a green coat of **basic copper carbonate**.
 
• **Aluminium Passivation:** Unlike iron, **aluminium** forms a very thin, tough layer of **aluminium oxide** that actually protects the rest of the metal from further corrosion.
 
 
 
• **Factors Influencing Corrosion:**
 
 
• **Moisture:** The presence of **water** or **humidity** is essential for the electrochemical process of **rusting**.
 
• **Salinity:** **Saltwater** (electrolytes) significantly speeds up the rate of **corrosion**, which is why ships and coastal structures deteriorate faster.
 
• **pH Levels:** Exposure to **acid rain** or acidic environments increases the **oxidation** rate of metals.
 
 
 
• **Prevention Methods:**
 
 
• **Galvanization:** Coating **iron** or **steel** with a thin layer of **zinc**. Even if the coating is scratched, **zinc** corrodes preferentially (sacrificial protection).
 
• **Electroplating:** Using **electricity** to coat a metal with a layer of another metal like **chromium** or **tin** to prevent **oxidation**.
 
• **Alloying:** Mixing metals with other elements. For example, **Stainless Steel** is an alloy of **iron**, **chromium**, and **nickel** that does not rust easily.
 
• **Painting and Greasing:** Applying a barrier of **paint**, **oil**, or **grease** to prevent the metal surface from coming into contact with **air** and **moisture**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Redox Reaction:** Corrosion is essentially a **redox** (reduction-oxidation) reaction. In **iron**, the metal acts as an **anode** and is **oxidized** to **Fe2+** ions, while **oxygen** is **reduced** at the **cathode**.
 
• **Economic Impact:** According to various global **surveys**, the **annual cost** of corrosion is estimated to be over **3%** of the global **GDP**, highlighting the importance of **anti-corrosion** technologies.
 
• **Microbial Corrosion:** Some types of corrosion are caused by **bacteria** (Sulphate-reducing bacteria) that can thrive in **pipelines** and **underground tanks**, leading to rapid **pitting** and failure.
